stem:
Dev compares three ways to count a large pile of beads: the spoken list one, two, three, … ; a list that stops at twenty; and a mark for each bead with no number words.

Which judgement is correct?

options.text: Call the stopping-at-twenty list an unending sequence, because it uses number words.
The spoken list one, two, three, … works even if he scrambles the order of the words.
The ordered list one, two, three, … keeps going and stays usable for large piles; the finite list stops, and single marks become cumbersome.
Choose the darkest bead in the pile as the count.

teacher.key_rationale: A useful count needs an unending ordered standard sequence. Stopping at twenty is finite. Scrambling drops order. Single marks continue but grow cumbersome. Bead colour is irrelevant.
